HOUSEZERO

By: Nicky Troll | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Imagine a home that is truly green, off the grid and an architectural triumph – now imagine parting with hundreds of thousands of rands, if not millions and having no home to show for it. We investi

Unique Selling Point:
** CLASSIC CARTE BLANCHE
** DODGY DEVELOPER CAUGHT OUT

Summary:

The man behind HouseZero is Yehoram Gur-arie - a quietly confident man with a big dream of building homes that have zero environmental impact – completely off the grid. The product is stunning, and Yehoram is charming and knowledgeable.

But no… Once you’ve signed on the dotted line, and parted with your cash, it’s not quite the dream green home you thought you signed up for. Actually, it’s not a home at all.

We speak to clients who got Zero Homes, insiders who worked for the company and a lawyer representing a group of HouseZero clients who have taken on the company legally.

Further information:
Yehoram Gur-arie has built a great digital presence for HouseZero – the website displays a number of different models, floor plans and pricing guides. He’s even been on the Home Channel with his designs and regularly posts on Social Media.

Customers have options when it comes to design, making your House Zero one of a kind. But once you’re hooked on the concept, it gets even better – you won’t have to wait months and months for the construction to be completed. This cutting-edge design is completed in a few weeks – from start to finish. From signing on the dotted line, you’ll be in your dream green home between 6 – 8 weeks. Wonderful right?

We have a list of at least 8 customers who have paid over R10 million and have waited in some cases close on 2 years for their dream green homes. In some cases materials have been delivered, in instances where some assembling has taken place the structure is not structurally sound.

These customers are angry – from pensioners to couples that have sold up and relocated to the coast to young couples starting out – they’ve all ended up with zero from House Zero.

But Yehoram is not one to accept defeat or take responsibility – he has fought these upset client despite being on the wrong side of these cases.

THE BASICS
1. PEOPLE WERE PROMISED HOMES IN A CERTAIN AMOUNT OF TIME
2. PEOPLE PAID OVER MONEY
3. PEOPLE DIDN’t GET THE HOMES THEY WERE PROMISED

In two of the cases there is blatant fraud – there are emails where two clients are told that their homes are ready to be transported and that they need to pay the balance. Yehoram even goes as far as saying that the house will arrive in 8 trucks, every two days. THOSE TRUCKS NEVER ARRIVED.

The same goes for the second client – the house was promised to be on a truck and heading to the Western Cape the following week – that was June 2020 – needless to say they don’t have a HouseZero – this particular couple have had to buy another home that has been bonded after they paid Yehoram’s company R1.9 million and got a half built structure that is uninhabitable.

ELEMENTS & INTERVIEWS

UNDERCOVER
I’ve gone undercover as a potential client to get the sales pitch and to get some footage of him in the bag. I was able to get a tour of the factory. He doesn’t over sell, he is just calm and confident. Nothing out there – but some footage.

** We will mention this in our interaction with him to cover ourselves.

CASE STUDY 1
Leon & Michelle Bosman – they paid R1.9 million for a home in Tergniet in the Western Cape – the have a half built structure. Some material has been damaged due the elements, they will need to spend a couple hundred thousand rand to complete it. They were contacted by a man interested in building a couple of these units – Yehoram told the potential client that the Bosman’s were difficult and didn’t want to show anyone their fabulous finished HouseZero – but the truth is they don’t have a finished home. Michelle is very animated and tells their story well.

We will interview them via Whatsapp Video call – but will have a cameraman on location in Tergniet filming the element.

CASE STUDY 2
Vassie Govender in Delmas. Vassie has a half built structure – she is a good option as we’ll be able to show the presenter at half built unit. Vassie started dealing with HouseZero in October 2019 – the building started in July 2020 – was meant to take 12 weeks. But here she is, R900k out of pocket and some materials to show for it, but no house to live in.

LAWYER
Dylan Jagga represents both the Bosman’s and a couple from Baviaanskloof – they don’t want to be on-camera and don’t want to be named but are happy for the lawyer to refer their case. They paid the most that we are aware of R5.4 million – they were blatantly defrauded. He has submitted over 300 pages as part of their legal proceedings, and has successfully been granted a court order that HouseZero should disclose their bank statements and assets – the company has not yet complied. Jagga believes this is because it will confirm the fraud – deposits were taken from a number of clients and the funds were not used for the intended purposes. This is also confirmed by a previous sub-contractor – who was using funds and materials from one building site to pay for another.

Dylan has been able to cross reference invoices and prove that money was taken from Paul to pay for Peter and has been able to show where HouseZero provided some clients invoices for materials as proof that their money was being used for the production of their homes, Dylan has been able to establish that those invoices were for other projects – MORE LIES CAUGHT OUT.

CONTRACTOR / FRANCHISEE
Floris Coetzee paid HouseZero R135k to buy into the company as a franchisee in the Western Cape – he did training with the company – but eventually pulled out after he was not getting payment for work done. Floris is a great layer – he could see that the pricing was wrong and that HouseZero could not deliver what they were selling at the prices they were charging. HE raised concerns about issues with the designs and was personally at a site in Pretoria that is now the flagship house where engineers detailed the structural issues and building challenges. Floris worked on four projects in 14 months – not one was completed.

We also have chatted to another sub-contractor that worked on 11 projects – not one was completed.

CONFRONT // RIGHT OF REPLY
We are going to call Yehoram from outside the factory and ask for an interview, we’ll explain we are there, that we have done undercover to hear the sales pitch and have had complaints from clients that say they’ve paid for a product they haven’t received. We’ll offer an interview for the next day, we’ll give him printed questions and take it from there.

If he declines, we’ll go back to do links which I’m sure will stir a little. And then we’ll wait for the legal letter.

FOOTAGE
We have website screen recordings, a youtube clip of the Home Channel piece, our undercover and visuals of the unfinished homes.

PLAN
I’m keeping it simple – HouseZero took cash, made blatant promises and failed to deliver – where is the house? Where is the money. Why did you lie?

Script:


STRUCTURE

VO: Imagine a home that is completely off the grid and architecturally modern and slick.

In a time where climate change is a genuine threat, and loadshedding is a reality for South Africans, consumers want to make greener choices, in an attempt to do right by the planet.

This dream, is what HouseZero is selling. A Pretoria company offering cutting-edge modular home designs, erected in a matter of weeks – from complete manufacture stage to moving in.

LINK: //Imagine spending hundreds of thousands, if not millions, of rands and not getting the green dream concept you thought, but rather an endless work in progress.

VO: That is what happened to these three HouseZero Clients.

Michelle Bosman opted for a double storey unit in Tergniet in the Western Cape back in July 2019. This is what just over R1.6 million bought the Bosmans. (R1619016.38)

MICHELLE: A nightmare is also a dream I, I realized, this the dream we had to stay here became an absolute nightmare.

VO: Vassie Govender chose a single story unit for her home in Delmas, Mpumalanga in October 2019. R868 000 in phase payments got Govender this unfinished structure. (R868207,49)

VASSIE: It's it's a constant reminder of a bad mistake.

VO: Robin Knox Grant decided on a compact single story unit for the garden of his Northcliff home in Johannesburg in February 2020.

ROBIN: I thought that's what I was going to get. I was wrong.

VO: Knox-Grant paid the full amount of R600 000 and got just this – a far cry from the impressive 3D drawings.

ROBIN: Big mistake. It never happens. It hasn't happened.

VO: The man behind HouseZero is Yoram Gur Arie - a seemingly confident man with a big dream of building modular homes that have zero environmental impact .

YORAM UPSOUND: Instead of using fresh municipal water for the toilet, we use water that is recycled.

VO: We met Yoram when we visited the HouseZero factory posing as a potential client.

YORAM: We normally budget 12 weeks for manufacturing and 12 weeks for work on site. //

LINK: The one thing that seals the deal for most clients is the time frames from breaking ground to completion. It should take around 12 weeks - would be super if it actually happens.

VO: We tracked down an additional 7 HouseZero clients – together they’ve paid over R11 million towards projects - most deadlines have not been met and not one of these homes have been completed.

Attorney Dylan Jagga represents some of these clients who have terminated their contracts and are suing the company in the hopes of getting some funds back.

DYLAN: There's a pattern in respect of the payment terms and requirements // once there, a certain milestone is reached in respect of payment, the progress // completely diminishes almost to a standstill.

VO: One of these clients is from Uniondale in the Eastern Cape. they’ve asked not to be named. The couple paid R5.427 million and was guaranteed delivery, by Yoram Gur Arie himself, by the 23rd of December 2020 .

DYLAN: // as early as 19 November 2020, there was an indication that the entire project was already complete and ready for delivery.

VO: This is the current state of the project in October 2021.

Similarly, the Bosmans were told in June 2020 that their home was ready for delivery. And asked to pay the “Complete Manufacture” invoice of R553 000 (R553776.75) .

MAC: the structure that I see behind it is that your beautiful new green home is everything finished.
MICHELLE: I’m laughing, but I promise if I’m not laughing I will be crying all the time. It is. It looks like a dilapidated chicken coop

VO: Bosman gave us a quick tour of the property, as it stands more than a year after paying the Complete Manufacture invoice.

MICHELLE: there’s something that can poke your eye out
MAC: This is crazy
MICHELLE: As you can see there is some glass lying everywhere…. they didn’t have the correct panels to affix it to. // This is really what we have after R1.6 million

VO: The Bosmans were given at least three different completion dates with materials arriving in random shipments from time to time.

MICHELLE: things arrive that couldn't, couldn't be used because. // they sent a truck full of pacifiers and every now and then a lollipop amongst the pacifiers.

VO: Vassie Govender had exactly the same experience. Since October 2019, she has had multiple completion dates, received materials in bits and pieces and dealt with a range of HouseZero employees who have come and gone .

VASSIE: It seems that they have high staff turnover // every project manager that comes out to site criticizes the work being done by the previous person.

VO: But what was said, and what was done, were often two very different things.

VASSIE: There’s been endless problems, // You can see that the workmanship is not up to standard. //I don't believe that the structure is stable at some of the metal sheeting is falling apart //

LINK: The House zero concept is great, but the execution is not always so great. It doesn't take an expert to see there are quite a few snags with the structure. One has to wonder could it be a case of the company going too big, too quickly?

FLORIS: they’ve bitten off more than they can chew.

VO: Floris Coetzee is a former HouseZero sub-contractor and construction partner

FLORIS: I think the problem was really to manufacturing with too slow and too small and on the design side needed more time to refine the product.

VO: He paid 50% of the R275000 fee to become the exclusive installer for all projects in the Western Cape. But a year into the partnership - Coetzee was having second thoughts when projects were falling behind and his cashflow was running dry .

FLORIS: By the end of end of the year, I had four projects in the pipeline and the first one was on 40 per cent, the other ones had not broken ground // This concept, you know, the way that they are running it is just not going to work for me. I will have to get out or borrow more money and go bankrupt.

VO: Eventually Coetzee halted work because of payment disputes. HouseZero then terminated the relationship.

Like some clients we spoke to, Knox Grant was promised a speedy installation. By paying up front, he got a discount and HouseZero endeavoured to erect the unit in just 6 weeks after completing manufacture. That’s half the USUAL timeframe.

ROBIN: // We can't live in that place. This was a disaster, an expensive disaster. The 600000 rand has come out of my pension money. I'll be 80 next year. No, it's a hell of a time of life to suddenly lose that amount of money out that you’ve saved in a pension fund.

VO: Interested to hear Yoram Gur Arie’s side of the story, we stopped by the HouseZero factory in Pretoria.

MAC: Hello. YORAM..// howzit guys, We'd like to see YORAM, please.

VO: Yoram tried real hard to avoid eye contact but he couldn’t escape our cameras….

MAC: Hey, YORAM (walks in)/I think you might be making him a bit uncomfortable.

VO: As Yoram vanished inside, the head of security scuttled over to speak on his boss’s behalf.

GUARD: he is busy with a conference call with Israel,
MAC: With Israel, Just just ask him, tell him, McFarlane Moleili from CB would like to see him
GUARD: he just told me to say he won’t be available
MAC: So he doesn't want to speak to us?
GUARD: probably

VO: Despite a number of emails and calls - Yoram declined the on-camera interview and sent through a written response.

Gur Arie admitted “that completion schedules have extended beyond the intended completion date with the above projects and some others” .

He also conceded that materials were delivered in bits and pieces, blaming the COVID-19 pandemic “This has delayed the delivery of all materials used in the manufacture and construction of our homes……. We have kept our clients updated on these unavoidable delays throughout.”

FLORIS: The lockdown didn't help, but even before after the lockdown, every single delivery was delayed from their side

VO: In terms of the structural soundness of the projects, Gur Arie STATES that “manufacturing mistakes can occur in any engineering project”. But SAYS - “...all HouseZero projects are signed off by a professional structural engineer and a professional architects as required by law and is certified accordingly”.

He had the following to add about the cases:

“...in all four cases the customers have been preventing HouseZero from completing the homes. We have had ongoing engagement with our clients in an attempt to complete the projects.”

DYLAN: It's very difficult to hear that version being put forward at all by House zero. // It's not correct insofar as the facts are concerned. Our clients have provided HouseZero with every opportunity to meet the the project, the undertakings in respect of the project. Some instances ranging to six or seven variations.

VO: Gur Arie insists project milestones had been reached in the four cases:

- In the Uniondale Couple’s Case - having received R5.427 million rand - Gur Arie admits they’ve paid in full for the material, but have only received 20 % of it, sighting “very challenging circumstances on the site, access to site [and] subcontractor performance”
- In the Bosmans’ Case he states 90% of material is on site and Construction is 80% complete.
- In Govender’s case - apparently 95% of material is on site and constructed. while Construction is 95% complete.
- In terms of Knox Grant - 90% of material is on site and constructed. WHile Construction is 80% complete according to Gur Arie.

ROBIN: // I'd call him a liar. // I would call him a thief because that's what I believe he is.

VO: Gur Arie further claimed in all four cases that he was still owed money for a portion of the construction that was done but not yet paid for. This, when he was paid more 80% by each of these clients and not one of their structures has a roof .

Interestingly, Gur Arie referred our undercover client to a home owned by the company, as an example of the HouseZero brand - it has a roof, is not yet complete either according to an estate agent marketing the house.

ESTATE AGENT CALL: It’s on the market for R4.164 million, and it is at the moment lets say 75% complete - cause why the developers want to meet the buyer to finish it accordingly, it’s not finished 100%.

ROBIN: It's probably the most unprofessional organization it's ever been my misfortune to deal with.

MICHELLE: I do think way in the beginning he had good intentions, but when the wheels came off, he didn't let anyone know.

VASSIE: It's not just the money, // we all don't have homes. What have we got to show? these people have violated us? And that is unforgivable.



STUDIO OUTTRO: HouseZero would like to be given the opportunity to complete these homes.

PROMOs

PROMO 1 (21 seconds)
VO: An off the grid home – that’s environmentally friendly, architecturally modern and slick, reasonably priced with a quick delivery timeframe – sounds fantastic.

ROBIN: // Big mistake. It never happens. It hasn't happened. M2M1

VO: We investigate a developer that sold big and failed to deliver.

PROMO 2 (21 seconds)
VO: A slick off the grid modular home appears to be great on paper, but doesn’t always manage to materialise as a finished project in real life – this despite clients paying hundreds of thousands of rands for their dream environmentally friendly homes.

ROBIN: // What I've received is a joke. // We can't live in that place. M7 This was a disaster, an expensive disaste

PROMO 3 (10 seconds)
VO: We investigate a developer that builds modern off the grid homes who appears to have sold big but failed to always deliver on a concept that hasn’t materialised in real life.

VO: Knox-Grant paid the full amount of R600 000 and got just this – a far cry from the impressive 3D drawings. ROBIN: Big mistake. It never happens. It hasn't happened. VO: The man behind HouseZero is Yoram Gur Arie - a seemingly confident man with a big dream of building modular homes that have zero environmental impact . YORAM UPSOUND: Instead of using fresh municipal water for the toilet, we use water that is recycled. VO: We met Yoram when we visited the HouseZero factory posing as a potential client. YORAM: We normally budget 12 weeks for manufacturing and 12 weeks for work on site. // LINK: The one thing that seals the deal for most clients is the time frames from breaking ground to completion. It should take around 12 weeks - would be super if it actually happens. VO: We tracked down an additional 7 HouseZero clients – together they’ve paid over R11 million towards projects - most deadlines have not been met and not one of these homes have been completed. Attorney Dylan Jagga represents some of these clients who have terminated their contracts and are suing the company in the hopes of getting some funds back. DYLAN: There's a pattern in respect of the payment terms and requirements // once there, a certain milestone is reached in respect of payment, the progress // completely diminishes almost to a standstill. VO: One of these clients is from Uniondale in the Eastern Cape. they’ve asked not to be named. The couple paid R5.427 million and was guaranteed delivery, by Yoram Gur Arie himself, by the 23rd of December 2020 . DYLAN: // as early as 19 November 2020, there was an indication that the entire project was already complete and ready for delivery. VO: This is the current state of the project in October 2021. Similarly, the Bosmans were told in June 2020 that their home was ready for delivery. And asked to pay the “Complete Manufacture” invoice of R553 000 (R553776.75) . MAC: the structure that I see behind it is that your beautiful new green home is everything finished. MICHELLE: I’m laughing, but I promise if I’m not laughing I will be crying all the time. It is. It looks like a dilapidated chicken coop VO: Bosman gave us a quick tour of the property, as it stands more than a year after paying the Complete Manufacture invoice. MICHELLE: there’s something that can poke your eye out MAC: This is crazy MICHELLE: As you can see there is some glass lying everywhere…. they didn’t have the correct panels to affix it to. // This is really what we have after R1.6 million VO: The Bosmans were given at least three different completion dates with materials arriving in random shipments from time to time. MICHELLE: things arrive that couldn't, couldn't be used because. // they sent a truck full of pacifiers and every now and then a lollipop amongst the pacifiers. VO: Vassie Govender had exactly the same experience. Since October 2019, she has had multiple completion dates, received materials in bits and pieces and dealt with a range of HouseZero employees who have come and gone . VASSIE: It seems that they have high staff turnover // every project manager that comes out to site criticizes the work being done by the previous person. VO: But what was said, and what was done, were often two very different things. VASSIE: There’s been endless problems, // You can see that the workmanship is not up to standard. //I don't believe that the structure is stable at some of the metal sheeting is falling apart // LINK: The House zero concept is great, but the execution is not always so great. It doesn't take an expert to see there are quite a few snags with the structure. One has to wonder could it be a case of the company going too big, too quickly? FLORIS: they’ve bitten off more than they can chew. VO: Floris Coetzee is a former HouseZero sub-contractor and construction partner FLORIS: I think the problem was really to manufacturing with too slow and too small and on the design side needed more time to refine the product. VO: He paid 50% of the R275000 fee to become the exclusive installer for all projects in the Western Cape. But a year into the partnership - Coetzee was having second thoughts when projects were falling behind and his cashflow was running dry . FLORIS: By the end of end of the year, I had four projects in the pipeline and the first one was on 40 per cent, the other ones had not broken ground // This concept, you know, the way that they are running it is just not going to work for me. I will have to get out or borrow more money and go bankrupt. VO: Eventually Coetzee halted work because of payment disputes. HouseZero then terminated the relationship. Like some clients we spoke to, Knox Grant was promised a speedy installation. By paying up front, he got a discount and HouseZero endeavoured to erect the unit in just 6 weeks after completing manufacture. That’s half the USUAL timeframe. ROBIN: // We can't live in that place. This was a disaster, an expensive disaster. The 600000 rand has come out of my pension money. I'll be 80 next year. No, it's a hell of a time of life to suddenly lose that amount of money out that you’ve saved in a pension fund. VO: Interested to hear Yoram Gur Arie’s side of the story, we stopped by the HouseZero factory in Pretoria. MAC: Hello. YORAM..// howzit guys, We'd like to see YORAM, please. VO: Yoram tried real hard to avoid eye contact but he couldn’t escape our cameras…. MAC: Hey, YORAM (walks in)/I think you might be making him a bit uncomfortable. VO: As Yoram vanished inside, the head of security scuttled over to speak on his boss’s behalf. GUARD: he is busy with a conference call with Israel, MAC: With Israel, Just just ask him, tell him, McFarlane Moleili from CB would like to see him GUARD: he just told me to say he won’t be available MAC: So he doesn't want to speak to us? GUARD: probably VO: Despite a number of emails and calls - Yoram declined the on-camera interview and sent through a written response. Gur Arie admitted “that completion schedules have extended beyond the intended completion date with the above projects and some others” . He also conceded that materials were delivered in bits and pieces, blaming the COVID-19 pandemic “This has delayed the delivery of all materials used in the manufacture and construction of our homes……. We have kept our clients updated on these unavoidable delays throughout.” FLORIS: The lockdown didn't help, but even before after the lockdown, every single delivery was delayed from their side VO: In terms of the structural soundness of the projects, Gur Arie STATES that “manufacturing mistakes can occur in any engineering project”. But SAYS - “...all HouseZero projects are signed off by a professional structural engineer and a professional architects as required by law and is certified accordingly”. He had the following to add about the cases: “...in all four cases the customers have been preventing HouseZero from completing the homes. We have had ongoing engagement with our clients in an attempt to complete the projects.” DYLAN: It's very difficult to hear that version being put forward at all by House zero. // It's not correct insofar as the facts are concerned. Our clients have provided HouseZero with every opportunity to meet the the project, the undertakings in respect of the project. Some instances ranging to six or seven variations. VO: Gur Arie insists project milestones had been reached in the four cases: - In the Uniondale Couple’s Case - having received R5.427 million rand - Gur Arie admits they’ve paid in full for the material, but have only received 20 % of it, sighting “very challenging circumstances on the site, access to site [and] subcontractor performance” - In the Bosmans’ Case he states 90% of material is on site and Construction is 80% complete. - In Govender’s case - apparently 95% of material is on site and constructed. while Construction is 95% complete. - In terms of Knox Grant - 90% of material is on site and constructed. WHile Construction is 80% complete according to Gur Arie. ROBIN: // I'd call him a liar. // I would call him a thief because that's what I believe he is. VO: Gur Arie further claimed in all four cases that he was still owed money for a portion of the construction that was done but not yet paid for. This, when he was paid more 80% by each of these clients and not one of their structures has a roof . Interestingly, Gur Arie referred our undercover client to a home owned by the company, as an example of the HouseZero brand - it has a roof, is not yet complete either according to an estate agent marketing the house. ESTATE AGENT CALL: It’s on the market for R4.164 million, and it is at the moment lets say 75% complete - cause why the developers want to meet the buyer to finish it accordingly, it’s not finished 100%. ROBIN: It's probably the most unprofessional organization it's ever been my misfortune to deal with. MICHELLE: I do think way in the beginning he had good intentions, but when the wheels came off, he didn't let anyone know. VASSIE: It's not just the money, // we all don't have homes. What have we got to show? these people have violated us? And that is unforgivable. STUDIO OUTTRO: HouseZero would like to be given the opportunity to complete these homes. PROMOs PROMO 1 (21 seconds) VO: An off the grid home – that’s environmentally friendly, architecturally modern and slick, reasonably priced with a quick delivery timeframe – sounds fantastic. ROBIN: // Big mistake. It never happens. It hasn't happened. M2M1 VO: We investigate a developer that sold big and failed to deliver. PROMO 2 (21 seconds) VO: A slick off the grid modular home appears to be great on paper, but doesn’t always manage to materialise as a finished project in real life – this despite clients paying hundreds of thousands of rands for their dream environmentally friendly homes. ROBIN: // What I've received is a joke. // We can't live in that place. M7 This was a disaster, an expensive disaste PROMO 3 (10 seconds) VO: We investigate a developer that builds modern off the grid homes who appears to have sold big but failed to always deliver on a concept that hasn’t materialised in real life.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Imagine a home that is truly green, off the grid and an architectural triumph – now imagine parting with hundreds of thousands of rands, if not millions and having no home to show for it. We investi
metadata.Unique Selling Point: ** CLASSIC CARTE BLANCHE ** DODGY DEVELOPER CAUGHT OUT
metadata.Summary: The man behind HouseZero is Yehoram Gur-arie - a quietly confident man with a big dream of building homes that have zero environmental impact – completely off the grid. The product is stunning, and Yehoram is charming and knowledgeable. But no… Once you’ve signed on the dotted line, and parted with your cash, it’s not quite the dream green home you thought you signed up for. Actually, it’s not a home at all. We speak to clients who got Zero Homes, insiders who worked for the company and a lawyer representing a group of HouseZero clients who have taken on the company legally.
metadata.Further information: Yehoram Gur-arie has built a great digital presence for HouseZero – the website displays a number of different models, floor plans and pricing guides. He’s even been on the Home Channel with his designs and regularly posts on Social Media. Customers have options when it comes to design, making your House Zero one of a kind. But once you’re hooked on the concept, it gets even better – you won’t have to wait months and months for the construction to be completed. This cutting-edge design is completed in a few weeks – from start to finish. From signing on the dotted line, you’ll be in your dream green home between 6 – 8 weeks. Wonderful right? We have a list of at least 8 customers who have paid over R10 million and have waited in some cases close on 2 years for their dream green homes. In some cases materials have been delivered, in instances where some assembling has taken place the structure is not structurally sound. These customers are angry – from pensioners to couples that have sold up and relocated to the coast to young couples starting out – they’ve all ended up with zero from House Zero. But Yehoram is not one to accept defeat or take responsibility – he has fought these upset client despite being on the wrong side of these cases. THE BASICS 1. PEOPLE WERE PROMISED HOMES IN A CERTAIN AMOUNT OF TIME 2. PEOPLE PAID OVER MONEY 3. PEOPLE DIDN’t GET THE HOMES THEY WERE PROMISED In two of the cases there is blatant fraud – there are emails where two clients are told that their homes are ready to be transported and that they need to pay the balance. Yehoram even goes as far as saying that the house will arrive in 8 trucks, every two days. THOSE TRUCKS NEVER ARRIVED. The same goes for the second client – the house was promised to be on a truck and heading to the Western Cape the following week – that was June 2020 – needless to say they don’t have a HouseZero – this particular couple have had to buy another home that has been bonded after they paid Yehoram’s company R1.9 million and got a half built structure that is uninhabitable. ELEMENTS & INTERVIEWS UNDERCOVER I’ve gone undercover as a potential client to get the sales pitch and to get some footage of him in the bag. I was able to get a tour of the factory. He doesn’t over sell, he is just calm and confident. Nothing out there – but some footage. ** We will mention this in our interaction with him to cover ourselves. CASE STUDY 1 Leon & Michelle Bosman – they paid R1.9 million for a home in Tergniet in the Western Cape – the have a half built structure. Some material has been damaged due the elements, they will need to spend a couple hundred thousand rand to complete it. They were contacted by a man interested in building a couple of these units – Yehoram told the potential client that the Bosman’s were difficult and didn’t want to show anyone their fabulous finished HouseZero – but the truth is they don’t have a finished home. Michelle is very animated and tells their story well. We will interview them via Whatsapp Video call – but will have a cameraman on location in Tergniet filming the element. CASE STUDY 2 Vassie Govender in Delmas. Vassie has a half built structure – she is a good option as we’ll be able to show the presenter at half built unit. Vassie started dealing with HouseZero in October 2019 – the building started in July 2020 – was meant to take 12 weeks. But here she is, R900k out of pocket and some materials to show for it, but no house to live in. LAWYER Dylan Jagga represents both the Bosman’s and a couple from Baviaanskloof – they don’t want to be on-camera and don’t want to be named but are happy for the lawyer to refer their case. They paid the most that we are aware of R5.4 million – they were blatantly defrauded. He has submitted over 300 pages as part of their legal proceedings, and has successfully been granted a court order that HouseZero should disclose their bank statements and assets – the company has not yet complied. Jagga believes this is because it will confirm the fraud – deposits were taken from a number of clients and the funds were not used for the intended purposes. This is also confirmed by a previous sub-contractor – who was using funds and materials from one building site to pay for another. Dylan has been able to cross reference invoices and prove that money was taken from Paul to pay for Peter and has been able to show where HouseZero provided some clients invoices for materials as proof that their money was being used for the production of their homes, Dylan has been able to establish that those invoices were for other projects – MORE LIES CAUGHT OUT. CONTRACTOR / FRANCHISEE Floris Coetzee paid HouseZero R135k to buy into the company as a franchisee in the Western Cape – he did training with the company – but eventually pulled out after he was not getting payment for work done. Floris is a great layer – he could see that the pricing was wrong and that HouseZero could not deliver what they were selling at the prices they were charging. HE raised concerns about issues with the designs and was personally at a site in Pretoria that is now the flagship house where engineers detailed the structural issues and building challenges. Floris worked on four projects in 14 months – not one was completed. We also have chatted to another sub-contractor that worked on 11 projects – not one was completed. CONFRONT // RIGHT OF REPLY We are going to call Yehoram from outside the factory and ask for an interview, we’ll explain we are there, that we have done undercover to hear the sales pitch and have had complaints from clients that say they’ve paid for a product they haven’t received. We’ll offer an interview for the next day, we’ll give him printed questions and take it from there. If he declines, we’ll go back to do links which I’m sure will stir a little. And then we’ll wait for the legal letter. FOOTAGE We have website screen recordings, a youtube clip of the Home Channel piece, our undercover and visuals of the unfinished homes. PLAN I’m keeping it simple – HouseZero took cash, made blatant promises and failed to deliver – where is the house? Where is the money. Why did you lie?
